newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH CBANK REPO RATE RISE FAILS TO BOOST CROWN.
newsitem.headline: CZECH CBANK REPO RATE RISE FAILS TO BOOST CROWN.

text.p: The Czech crown slipped in early trading on Friday, after a 50 basis point rise in the central bank's (CNB) repo rate failed to shore up market sentiment, dealers said.
Late on Thursday the CNB said it had decided to raise its repo rate, but had not set a target for how much it would rise instead allowing "market conditions" to be the determining factor.
Early on Friday the CNB then announced a one-week repo tender at 12.9 percent, up from 12.4 percent.
Dealers said they thought the move was far too little to provide any real support for the crown.

"I don't think such a change in rates will effect the market at all. If the central bank is going to protect the crown it has to do something more significant, not just a few basis points," said Breta Tichanek of ING bank.
Just before the repo rate change, the crown was trading at 3.84 percent on the depreciation side of its dollar/mark basket parity. After the announcement, the crown slipped to -3.93 percent.
On Thursday, the crown was fixed at 30.673 against the dollar and 18.177 against the mark implying a deviation of -3.40 percent.

Thursday's rate announcement came after the crown plunged to a record low of five percent on the depreciation side of its dollar/mark basket parity, prompting the CNB to intervene on the market to support the currency for the first time in over a year.
